title: onprem-airgap-offline-bundle-vendor-rke2-ubuntu-22.04-tuf-mirror-tooling
author: Aisha Patel
body: Summary: Add updated on-prem/air-gapped offline bundle for RKE2 on Ubuntu 22.04 with TUF metadata mirroring and revert/rollback tooling. This PR vendors required distro artifacts, refreshes Flatcar/RKE2 compatibility matrices, updates Helm charts used by the private installer, and adds a small Terraform module tweak to surface mirror endpoint configuration. Motivation: customers running air-gapped installs on Ubuntu 22.04 and Flatcar were hitting TUF metadata expiration and missing upstream mirrors for certain kernels/containerd packages. The new mirror tooling makes it possible to generate a complete offline bundle and also to perform a safe rollback of TUF metadata in case of a bad mirror push. Changes: - offline-bundles/vendor/rke2/ubuntu-22.04: add vendored packages (kernel, containerd, rke2 binary), updated manifests and checksums - offline-bundles/vendor/rke2/flatcar: pin Flatcar images and add systemd drop-in for compatibility - tooling/mirror-tuf.sh: new script that mirrors TUF metadata and package blobs into a local HTTP server, supports incremental sync and manifest signing - tooling/revert-tuf.sh: tooling to revert to previous TUF snapshot and regenerate repository metadata for clients - helm/redwood-private/values-airgap.yaml: add mirror configuration and TLS bootstrap options - terraform/modules/private_installer/mirror: expose mirror_url and ttl configuration, add acceptance tests for URL validation - installer: improvements to archive layout and verification to reduce installer memory at runtime Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag; initial customers will opt-in and provide a read-only mirror endpoint. Extensive verification steps included in this PR. Backwards compatibility: existing bundles still supported; installer will pick vendor bundle by distro label. Testing: unit tests for mirror tooling, local end-to-end airgap runbook verified in a lab cluster (rke2 v1.28 and flatcar stable), manual TUF key rotation simulation. Checklist: - [x] Vendored artifacts collected and checksummed - [x] TUF metadata signing integrated into mirror script - [x] Helm values documented - [x] Terraform module updated + unit tests - [x] e2e airgap smoke run (lab) - [x] Security review for vendored binaries Notes: This description intentionally includes the full changelog summary and upgrade notes. See commits and review conversation for more context.

b12c9e1: tooling: add mirror-tuf.sh with incremental sync and signing options
e7f3b44: tooling: add revert-tuf.sh and snapshot management helpers
c4a9d21: helm: add mirror_url config and tls_bootstrap option for airgap installs
d59ab77: terraform: expose mirror_url and ttl in private_installer module; add validator test
f2e6c90: installer: archive layout fix to reduce memory during extraction
9d3f5b0: docs: update INSTALL-AIRGAP.md with mirror steps and rollback instructions
review_comments: Connor Lee (2026-02-16): Left a few comments on mirror-tuf.sh - can we make the HTTP client respect system proxy settings and add retries with exponential backoff? Also please add a small unit test that simulates a 503 transient error.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-16): Thanks — added retry logic and a test that injects a 503 response. Also documented proxy behavior in the script header.
Devon Martinez (2026-02-18): Helm values look good; request to add default tls_bootstrap=false and a note about using an init container when TLS certs are pre-populated.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-18): Updated values-airgap.yaml to default tls_bootstrap to false and added a paragraph in INSTALL-AIRGAP.md about init containers for cert bootstrapping.

Sofia Alvarez (2026-02-19): Security review: vendor assessment looks mostly fine but we need provenance for the rke2 binary and containerd. Please add a short note about how artifacts were obtained and verified.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-19): Added VENDOR-ASSESSMENT.md with provenance steps and GPG signatures where available.
Connor Lee (2026-02-20): One nit: archive layout change reduced memory but made extraction order non-deterministic; can we add a deterministic sort when creating tar streams?
Aisha Patel (2026-02-21): Fixed: tar stream generation now sorts entries by path before packing. Added test in installer package.
CI Bot (2026-02-21): ci/pipelines/mirror-tooling.yml failed on first run: unit tests timed out in acceptance/mirror-module-validate_test.go; retriggering.
CI Bot (2026-02-22): All checks passed on rerun. Ready for merge.
Devon Martinez (2026-02-22): Approving after CI green and documentation updates.
Connor Lee (2026-02-22): Approved. Small follow-up: we should add a cron to the mirror runner in the next PR to handle auto refresh cadence.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-22): Noted — will follow up with a scheduled-runner PR.
release_notes: - Add Ubuntu 22.04 and Flatcar vendor bundles for RKE2 (air-gapped installs); - Mirror tooling (mirror-tuf.sh) for mirroring TUF metadata and package blobs locally; - Revert tooling (revert-tuf.sh) to rollback TUF snapshots; - Helm and Terraform updates to configure mirror endpoints and TLS bootstrap; - Installer memory reduction and deterministic archive layout; - Security vendor assessment and provenance documentation.
